Action Plan:
1. Suspected viral upper respiratory tract infection (sore throat, dry cough, mild exertional dyspnoea, transient fever): provide symptomatic care (paracetamol dose/route/frequency not documented, encourage adequate fluids and rest); advise red-flag review if breathlessness worsens, new chest pain, haemoptysis, persistent fever, or no improvement within 4–5 days.
2. Issue electronic sick note to cover additional days off work as discussed.
3. Reassure regarding low likelihood of tuberculosis or lung cancer at present; advise follow-up with GP if symptoms persist or progress.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting with 1-week history of sore throat (onset last Thu/Fri) followed 1–2 days later by dry cough.  
• Developed mild shortness of breath 3–4 days ago; noticeable on walking/exercise but not limiting daily activities; no dyspnoea at rest.  
• Reports “a bit” of wheeze and chest discomfort (conflict noted: later denies chest pain).  
• Feverish for first 3 days; afebrile since.  
• Intermittent headaches early in illness, now resolved.  
• Reduced appetite; no weight loss.  
• No nasal congestion, no sputum, no haemoptysis, no rash.  
Past medical history: none.  
Surgical history: not discussed.  
Medications: none.  
Allergies: peanuts.  
Family history: mother – lung cancer; no family history of thromboembolism.  
Social: Non-smoker (occasional experimental use “once or twice”); no known asbestos exposure; employed; born USA, living in UK ≥12 years; recent travel limited to Europe.  

Objective:
• No physical examination performed (video limits; patient unable to demonstrate throat view).  
• Patient denies palpable neck lumps.  
• No vital signs or investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Upper respiratory tract infection (viral pharyngitis/acute bronchitis)
   - Assessment: Likely self-limiting viral URTI with reactive cough and mild exertional dyspnoea.  
   - Differential: Early lower respiratory tract infection, COVID-19 (not discussed), asthma, atypical pneumonia.  
   - Investigations: None at present; advised to seek face-to-face GP review if deterioration or lack of improvement.  
   - Treatment: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for fever/pain; hydration; rest.  
   - Safety-net: Return/seek urgent care for increasing breathlessness, persistent/worsening symptoms >4–5 days, chest pain, haemoptysis, or new systemic symptoms.

2. Sick leave certificate
   - Assessment: Illness impacting work attendance.  
   - Treatment: Provide sick note for additional days as requested.

3. Health anxiety regarding tuberculosis and lung cancer
   - Assessment: Concern understandable given family history; current presentation does not suggest serious pathology.  
   - Treatment: Reassurance given; advised to re-present if symptoms persist or escalate.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs, respiratory examination, or throat visualization; medication reconciliation limited; immunization history not obtained.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially denies then later confirms shortness of breath; states both presence and absence of chest pain. DOB 09-May-2016 inconsistent with adult history (age conflict).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor overlaps and incomplete phrases but clinically usable.
